seny

Sanity checks for differential gene Expression in NoisY data (and seny, the Catalan word for common sense).

For every cluster-by-contrast comparison in a multi-sample single-cell dataset, seny decides whether a pseudobulk differential-expression test is Adequate, Underpowered, Caution or Invalid, and explains why. The diagnostics are analytic and run on your own data — there is no per-dataset simulation.

Call Meaning
Invalid Type I error cannot be trusted (design not estimable, too few samples per group).
Caution Valid, but a risk applies (condition confounded with a covariate, or cell-count imbalance tracking the condition).
Underpowered Valid but unable to detect the target effect (sensitivity too low, or too few testable genes).
Adequate No flags.

The call has a severity order — Invalid > Caution > Underpowered > Adequate — and a reason string that lists every flag, so a single headline never hides a second problem.

Installation

seny is not yet on Bioconductor. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("smorabit/seny")

Usage 

library(seny)

sce <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "example_sce.rds", package = "seny"))

res <- assessAll(sce, sample = "donor", group = "condition",
                 annotations = "cell_type", targetLFC = 1)
res                         # one row per comparison: metrics, call, reason

plots <- plotAdequacy(res)  # traffic-light matrix, one ggplot per annotation set
plots[["cell_type"]]

See vignette("seny") for the full walk-through.

Status

Experimental (P1 MVP). The package covers diagnostic layers 1, 2 and 4; the call thresholds in defaultThresholds() are provisional placeholders being recalibrated from a validation study (OneK1K, AIDA and an in-house atlas). Outlier detection, empirical checks, composition assessment, calibrated power and an HTML report are planned.
